summary: Preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes 727KB obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a Vue dropdown UI component but ships a preinstall script (setup.mjs) that, on npm install, downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases (bun-v1.3.13, platform/arch-selected zip), extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it to run a 727KB sibling file math_init.js bundled with the package. math_init.js is a Bun-CJS module obfuscated with string-array rotation (a WV8StW shift routine), integer-indexed lookup tables, and _0xNNNN-style identifier mangling, with no readable API surface. The setup.mjs script itself uses the same _0xNNNN obfuscation style to construct the Bun download URL and the execFileSync call. A Vue dropdown component has no legitimate need for an alternate JavaScript runtime or an opaque half-megabyte native-executed payload at install time. The overall shape — install-time fetch of an alien runtime used specifically to execute a locally shipped, heavily obfuscated payload that Node-based tooling cannot inspect — is an alternate-runtime dropper designed to run attacker-controlled code on the installer's build host while evading Node-level analysis.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
